scenario.description: A department head must decide whether Mara should lead the next employee-onboarding cohort and finalize the support, workload, and interpersonal safeguards for the assignment.

shared_context.S1: The department will run a six-week onboarding cohort for eight new employees beginning next month.
shared_context.S2: Mara is one of the employees being considered to lead the cohort.
shared_context.S3: Elena makes the binding decision about the cohort lead and the operating plan.
shared_context.S4: At the final planning meeting, Elena's normal process is to hear a round-robin report from the team lead, Mara, a peer colleague, and HR before finalizing the plan. Each participant must explicitly enter any relevant report as a disclosure during their turn so it is on the record.
shared_context.S5: Department policy requires cohort plans to document any workload limitation, observed readiness evidence, interpersonal concern, or applicable HR requirement before approval.
shared_context.S6: The approval plan records follow-up commitments using these categories when applicable: readiness_evidence_documentation, workload_limitation_documentation, facilitated_feedback, backup_coverage, and manager_checkins. Elena's approval record names the source of each reported item in its justification.

PF1.text: Jonah directly observed Mara co-facilitate four onboarding sessions over the past quarter, and she handled difficult participant questions independently; he has not submitted this observation in the formal readiness review.

PF2.text: Mara has a standing caregiving arrangement that limits her cohort-lead work to exactly 3 hours per week and makes her unavailable for Friday sessions; she has not raised it because the assignment has not yet been offered.

PF3.text: Priya personally witnessed exactly two meetings in which Mara was interrupted and excluded from the facilitation handoff; Priya believes the assignment should include a facilitated feedback meeting, but has not put the incidents in a formal report.

PF4.text: Luis confirmed with Employee Relations this week that a first-time cohort lead must have a named backup and weekly manager check-ins for exactly 6 weeks; he was waiting for the policy interpretation to be confirmed before bringing it to Elena.

acceptance_conditions: Mara must be appointed cohort lead and Jonah's observed facilitation evidence must be recorded.
The assignment must be limited to exactly 3 hours per week with no Friday sessions.
The plan must record exactly two exclusion incidents and require a facilitated feedback meeting.
A named backup and weekly manager check-ins for exactly 6 weeks must be included.
The settlement must include commitments for facilitated feedback, backup coverage, and six weeks of manager check-ins.

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in revealed and 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids
provenance_checks.P2: 'PF2' in revealed and 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids
provenance_checks.P3: 'PF3' in revealed and 'PF3' in credited_facts and 'PF3' in justification_fact_ids
provenance_checks.P4: 'PF4' in revealed and 'PF4' in credited_facts and 'PF4' in justification_fact_ids

decisive_facts.why: Jonah's four independently handled onboarding sessions change the decision from an unsupported appointment to appointing Mara with her facilitation evidence recorded.
Mara's caregiving arrangement changes the workload to exactly 3 hours per week and changes Friday sessions from allowed to prohibited.
Priya's observation changes the plan to require a facilitated feedback meeting and records the incident count as exactly 2.
Employee Relations' confirmed requirement changes the plan to include a named backup and manager check-ins lasting exactly 6 weeks, with corresponding backup and manager-check-in commitments.
